rows.description: A wise person asks which choice she will respect in ten years, accepts that some regret is normal, and commits fully once she chooses.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child feels less guilty for letting a wrong happen than for causing it. Harm by inaction seems milder than the same harm by action.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who sees a classmate being teased stays silent, feeling less responsible than the teaser. Doing nothing feels safer than intervening, but the harm still occurs.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult avoids a recommended vaccine or check-up because a rare side effect feels worse than a larger risk from the disease. Action feels more blameworthy than inaction.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A mature person asks what she would think if she had caused the outcome directly, accepts that not acting is also a choice, and speaks up or seeks qualified advice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager prefers removing a small risk entirely over greatly cutting a larger one, because getting to zero feels comforting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student accepts a low but sure return over a much better one, or fixates on eliminating one small fear while ignoring a bigger danger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A careful planner asks how much overall risk is reduced by each option and does not fixate on the comfort of a perfect zero.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young parent notices relatives over-protect from one rare risk while overlooking common ones, and helps choose measures by total benefit with kindness toward the fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler told not to touch something reaches for it at once. Being restricted makes the forbidden thing more attractive and he asserts his own will.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
